Exact rules
Slots touching above, below, left, or right are adjacent; diagonal slots are not.
Front and behind follow the same three-slot row. Above and below follow the same column.
Opposite targets the mirrored slot on the enemy board.
Link Cable is the explicit exception that considers every Batomon on your team adjacent to each other.
3×2 adjacency
Top left · Adjacent Top middle · Selected Top right · Adjacent Bottom left · Diagonal Bottom middle · Adjacent Bottom right · Diagonal
From the top-middle slot, top-left, top-right, and bottom-middle are adjacent.
Bottom-left and bottom-right are diagonal from top-middle, so they are not adjacent.
The mirrored enemy top-middle slot is opposite top-middle.

At 1.0 seconds: deal 3, then fall to 2 Burn.

References.Title: Charge
References.Text:
Current mechanic
Charge
Charge advances a Batomon toward its next cast by the stated number of seconds.
Balance 25 Steam build 25738032
Exact rules
Charge adds the printed number of seconds to current cast progress.
At the next cooldown check, reaching the cooldown queues one sequence, resets progress, and discards excess Charge. If Knockout cancels that timed cast before it executes, the game can restore the spent progress.
For a 1-second cooldown, one 3-second Charge starts one sequence, not three. With Multicast 1, that means one cast; no 2-second remainder survives.
Multicast still controls the number of casts within that sequence. Extra casts from Multicast are not extra cooldown completions from excess Charge.
Charge does not reset or change base cooldown, added cooldown, or Cooldown Speed.
Dracana and Ironcore cannot receive Charge, including from other sources.

Common questions
What happens if a 1-second cooldown receives 3 seconds of Charge? The next cooldown check starts one cast sequence and resets progress to zero. With Multicast 1, it casts once. The excess 2 seconds are discarded, not saved for later casts.

References.Title: Monster pool & shop
References.Text:
Current mechanic
Monster pool & shop
A normal shop has five slots, uses rank-based rarity odds, and rolls from your run's species roster.
Balance 25 Steam build 25738032
Exact rules
A normal shop has five slots. Four offer Batomon. The fifth offers an eligible Item when the Item budget allows it, or a Batomon otherwise. Berroon's banked Berries can keep that slot active after the usual budget is spent.
The daily Item budget starts at 1. Berries refund their use. Tote Bag adds 2 uses today, and Membership Card adds 1 each day. Berroon banks Berry offers rather than extra daily uses.
A normal reroll replaces all five slots. It costs $3 unless a free reroll is available, in which case one free reroll is spent first.
Free rerolls can carry into later shops. Fake Coin grants 1, and Youngster grants 3 each day. Membership Card adds an Item use, not a free reroll.
Locking is free and carries the current contents into the next day. The lock then clears, and any empty bought slots are refilled.
A normal reroll clears both the visible lock and the next-day carry flag. Lock the new contents again to retain them.
The run begins at Shop Rank 1 and gains 1 rank at the start of every day. Basic Bait lowers rank by 1 but not below 1; Apex Bait, Market License, Lady, and some events add rank.
Base rank odds never include Mythical. The highest base rarity is Common at Rank 1, Uncommon at Ranks 2–3, Rare at 4–5, Super Rare at 6–8, and Legendary at Rank 9 or higher.
The percentages shown in the shop use the final normalized weights after effects such as VIP Pass or Research Notes change them.
Offers are generated independently for each run. Buying a Batomon does not remove a finite copy from the pool, so the same species can appear repeatedly or in multiple slots.
Normal offers use the run's species roster. It starts from the selected region's set unless the run specifies a roster. Effects can add species to that roster. Availability tags alone do not define the pool.
Normal rolls exclude species owned at Level 3 or above on the team or bench, plus their listed base species. Swoonet is exempt. An empty rarity pool falls back to lower rarities.
The normal shiny chance is 1 in 200 per rolled Batomon. Shiny-chance bonuses multiply that base chance; Lucky Girl changes it to 10%.
Rainbow Pearl turns current and future shop Batomon shiny when that species has a shiny form.
Buying uses the offer's current price, places the Batomon in a requested empty slot or the first team slot, then the first bench slot, and applies purchase effects before checking merges.
The team holds 6 Batomon and the bench holds 4. If all 10 slots are full and the purchase cannot merge immediately, it enters overflow; reroll, lock, and battle stay disabled until overflow is cleared.
Ordinary merges use three Level 1 copies for Level 2, then two Level 2 copies for Level 3. Swoonet needs two copies per level and merges further. Grow Lamp reduces the Level 1 requirement for Grass Batomon. Shared groups include Riglet/Rigalord, Pipskull/Ratacomb, Emberpaw/Oniclaw, Kindlepot/Furnadon, and Sproutquill/Fernfowl/Quillustrous.
A merge keeps the strongest permanent bonus for each stat rather than adding matching bonuses, combines added types and stored discounts, and becomes shiny if any ingredient is shiny.
Ordinary merges stop at Level 3. Upgrade Disc levels a bought Batomon below Level 3 once. Mega Upgrade Disc adds a level when a Batomon reaches Level 3. Swoonet merges beyond Level 4. Kappow gains levels after victories and can also exceed Level 4.
Sell value is ceil((base cost × level factor + stored purchase discounts) ÷ 2), plus bonus Sell Value, with a zero floor. Ordinary factors are 1 at Level 1, 3 at Level 2, and 6 at Level 3 or above. Swoonet uses 1, 2, and 4 instead.
A rarity Ticket replaces all five slots with Batomon rolls of its chosen rarity, spends no normal or free reroll, and still uses normal set, maxed-species, fallback, shiny, and spawn effects.
Ticket rolls clear the shop lock and its next-day carry flag. They also activate effects such as Cosmivore from discarded Batomon. Echo Bell repeats a zero-cost Ticket effect without another Item use.
Research Notes adds 20 Legendary weight. VIP Pass sets Common and Uncommon weight to zero and forces Rare weight when no higher base weight remains.
Mystic Incense queues a Mythical from the run's roster and is consumed when that Batomon enters the shop. It can fill an empty slot in a retained shop. Base rank odds never roll Mythical.
Each Faebloom gives the Item slot a 10% chance to become Mythical. Shopkeeper raises rolled Item tier by 1, capped at Mythical, and discounts Items by 15%; both effects stack with additional copies.
Coupon discounts each current Batomon offer by $3. Effects such as Bug Net, Chef, Rainbow Pearl, and the shop Bells modify eligible offers. Persistent offer bonuses remain after purchase. Bug Catcher makes the first Bug purchase each day free.
Voucher recruits a current offer for free and counts as a purchase. Lootbox and Recruiting Flyer use non-purchase grants. Lootbox grants a Legendary, and Recruiting Flyer grants a Level 3 Uncommon.
When a shop is rerolled, Cosmivore permanently gains a percentage of the discarded Batomon's combined Damage, Heal, Shield, Burn, Poison, and Shock; bought or empty slots contribute nothing.

Batomon Cosmivore
Level 1 When rerolling the shop, gain 20% of the total stats of the monsters remaining in the shop (excluding Multicast and Cooldown).
Cosmivore gains permanent stats from Batomon discarded by a reroll.
Common questions
How many slots are in the shop? There are five. Four offer Batomon. The last offers an eligible Item when the budget allows it, or another Batomon otherwise. Berroon's banked Berries can still appear after the normal daily uses are spent.
Is the monster pool shared or depleted when someone buys a Batomon? No. Each run uses its own species roster, and purchases do not deplete a finite supply. Normal rolls exclude Level 3-or-higher species on the team or bench and their listed base forms, except Swoonet.
How do shop odds progress? Shop Rank starts at 1, rises by 1 each day, and uses the full Rank 1 through Rank 14+ table above. Effects can then modify and renormalize those base weights.
Can Mythical Batomon appear in a normal Shop Rank roll? No. Base rank odds stop at Legendary. Mythical shop offers come from special effects such as Crimson Ticket or Mystic Incense; other effects, such as Gamer, grant a Mythical directly instead of offering it for purchase.
What does locking the shop do? It retains the contents for the next day for free and refills empty slots. A normal reroll clears the lock and the next-day carry flag. Lock the new contents again if you want to retain them.
How much does a reroll cost? A normal reroll costs $3. If you have free rerolls, it costs $0 and consumes one free reroll; unused free rerolls remain available later.
Which Batomon can appear in the default shop? The run's species roster controls normal offers. The selected region provides the usual starting roster, and some effects add species. A run can also specify its roster directly. Availability tags alone do not control normal offers. The current catalog contains 148 species. Pantra has 81 species and Jinto has 85, with some shared species.
When do copies merge? Ordinary merges use three Level 1 copies for Level 2, then two Level 2 copies for Level 3. Grow Lamp reduces the Level 1 requirement for Grass Batomon. Swoonet merges from two copies at every level. Kappow can gain levels beyond 4 after victories.
How is sell value calculated? Multiply base cost by 1 at Level 1, 3 at Level 2, or 6 at Level 3 and above. Add stored purchase discounts, divide by 2, round up, and add bonus Sell Value. The result cannot be negative. Swoonet uses factors 1, 2, and 4 instead.
What is the normal shiny chance in the shop? Each normal Batomon roll has a 1-in-200 shiny chance. Lucky Girl raises that to 10%, and Rainbow Pearl makes shop Batomon shiny whenever that species has a shiny form.

If the purchase causes merges, On Bought waits for the merge chain. It uses the surviving Batomon's On Bought ability and resulting level.
Echo Charm adds one activation. The game adds these repeat bonuses to the normal single activation.
Not every acquisition counts as a purchase. Lootbox and Recruiting Flyer use the non-purchase path; Voucher explicitly counts as a purchase.
An effect can explicitly activate On Bought without a new purchase. Gemwing does this to the ally above when Gemwing casts.
Gemwing activates that ability 1, 2, 3, or 12 times at Levels 1–4, multiplied by one plus the On Bought repeat bonuses.
On Bought is separate from effects that react when another Batomon is bought. It is not an ordinary cooldown cast.

Common questions
Does receiving a free Batomon always activate On Bought? No. The acquisition must count as a purchase, or an effect must explicitly activate On Bought. Voucher counts as a purchase; Lootbox and Recruiting Flyer do not.

Current mechanic

On Cast resolves whenever that Batomon performs a cast.

The normal post-battle phase applies On Victory rewards after a win. Black Belt can activate a lone Fighting Batomon's On Victory ability at battle start.

References.Title: Shock
References.Text:
Current mechanic
Shock
Direct Damage triggers a separate Shock hit equal to the target's Shock stacks; Shock stays until removed.
Balance 25 Steam build 25738032
Exact rules
When direct Damage hits a team with Shock, Shock deals a separate hit equal to the current Shock stack count.
That Shock hit resolves before the direct hit, so it reaches Shield first.
Shock applied by a cast does not affect that same cast's direct Damage because status application follows Damage.
Shock does not decay naturally.
Burn, Poison, Shock, and Sudden Death damage do not trigger another Shock hit.
If Shield is present, the triggered Shock hit is reduced by 15% before Shield absorbs it.
Direct hit example
Without Shield: 30 direct Damage + 5 Shock = 35 damage This example has no damage modifiers. Shock resolves first as a separate hit and does not trigger another Shock hit.

References.Title: Stat Caps
References.Text:
Current mechanic
Stat Caps
Combat output stats, their percentage bonuses, Cooldown Speed, and the stat-gain multiplier use the 999,999,999 cap.
Balance 25 Steam build 25738032
Exact rules
Cooldown Speed and the stat-gain multiplier also use this cap. String-based values, such as bonus Sell Value, use separate rules.
Those capped combat stats cannot increase beyond 999,999,999.
Cooldown and Multicast use separate rules: effective cooldown has a 0.1-second minimum and Multicast has a minimum of 1.
The combat-stat cap does not establish a cap for team HP, gold, shop values, or unrelated systems.

References.Title: Sudden Death
References.Text:
Current mechanic
Sudden Death
Sudden Death begins at 30 battle seconds, then a sandstorm damages both teams every 0.5 seconds.
Balance 25 Steam build 25738032
Exact rules
Sudden Death begins when the battle timer reaches 30 seconds.
The first sandstorm hit follows after 0.5 seconds, and hits continue every 0.5 seconds.
Damage follows 8 × 2^(seconds active ÷ 3), doubling every 3 seconds.
Shield absorbs Sudden Death damage, but the 15% Shield reduction for Burn, Poison, and Shock does not apply to it.
The damage scales continuously while the popup shows a whole-number value.
Sandstorm curve
damage = 8 × 2^(seconds active ÷ 3) The curve doubles every 3 active seconds; damage is applied on each 0.5-second tick.

References.Title: Team HP
References.Text:
Current mechanic
Team HP
Each side fights with one shared HP total rather than separate HP for every Batomon.
Balance 25 Steam build 25738032
Exact rules
Damage lowers shared team HP after Shield is exhausted.
Heal restores shared team HP without exceeding that battle's maximum.
Shield protects shared team HP by absorbing incoming damage first.
The HP bar never shows less than 0, but Damage can take the real team HP below 0.
Same-tick Heal adds to that real value. At 300 HP, 307 Damage leaves -7 HP, so a 30 Heal on that tick leaves 23 HP, not 30.
The winner check runs after Heal. A team survives the tick only if its real HP is above 0 after Heal.
If both teams end the same tick at 0 HP or less after ordered effects resolve, the player is awarded the win.
Shared defense
Shield absorbs incoming damage.
Remaining damage lowers the team's HP bar.
Heal restores that same HP bar after the ordered same-tick effects.
Current build examples
Batomon Pebbler
Level 1 On Cast · +15 Shield for this battle.
Pebbler supplies Shield for the shared defense layer.
Item Mystic Pearl
Give your Water monsters +10 Heal.
Mystic Pearl increases Heal on current Water Batomon.
Common questions
Why did a 30 Heal bring my team back to only 23 HP after the bar showed 0? The bar stops at 0, but the real HP was -7 after 307 Damage hit 300 HP. Heal adds to -7, so the team has 23 HP and survives the tick.

References.Title: How to play Batomon Showdown
References.Text:
New player guide
How to play Batomon Showdown
Batomon Showdown is an asynchronous auto-battler: build a team of up to six, then fight a saved board from the same day. A normal run ends at 10 wins or when your lives finally run out.
Build in the shop. Battle automatically. Reach 10 wins before your lives run out.
What a run is
A run alternates between an untimed shop and automatic battles. A normal run ends at 10 wins or when your life pool is exhausted after its one Second Chance.
You field up to six Batomon. They share one battle HP pool, so individual Batomon can be knocked out while the side keeps fighting until that shared HP reaches zero.
Runs start with 10 lives. A loss costs 1 life on days 1–2, 2 lives on days 3–4, and 3 lives from day 5 onward.
The first time your lives fall to zero, Second Chance puts you back on 1 life and opens a reward event. The next depletion ends the run, so there is no fixed five-loss limit.
Take as long as you need in the shop. Once you choose Battle, buying and positioning stop and the prepared boards resolve without tactical turn-by-turn input.
Exact rules: Team hp Knockout Sudden death
Battles play automatically, and each side fights with one shared HP bar. Second Chance returns you to 1 life the first time your lives hit zero.
Who you fight
You fight saved boards from the same numbered day, not a live opponent. The tutorial can use authored opponents instead.
The game normally selects opponents from downloaded bundles for your region and mode. Ranked bundles also use MMR brackets. Cached bundles permit offline selection.
The current search first tries humans from Balance 24–25, then older compatible boards. Within each search step, it prefers Balance 25.
Casual prefers a human at or below your casual MMR, then any casual human, then a ranked human. Before your first 10-win run, it has a 30% bot-first chance at 7 wins or fewer. The tutorial has separate rules.
Ranked tries a ±1000 MMR band on day 1. Later days try ±200, then ±500, then ±1000, then any eligible ranked human.
Bronze through Platinum initially exclude Master boards, then remove that restriction if necessary. Diamond and Master do not use that restriction.
The search first avoids humans already faced in the run. It can then accept a different run from that player, up to two matches per player. The search can cross between Casual and Ranked. If necessary, it later removes the rematch restriction, then tries bots. If no compatible bundled board remains, the game can copy your own board.
A board with the ??? trainer does not enter matchmaking. Outside Extended Mode, a run that held a Mythical is withheld unless Ranked and Master. A current team with Dirgefin, Reapra, or Celestia is withheld unless you are Master.
The game can try up to three candidates to avoid a Mythical you have not encountered. It can accept the third candidate even if that candidate still has one. Candidate selection also reduces the chance of certain hard counters to your board.
Outside Extended Mode, the game can reduce permanent buffs, levels, and trinkets, or remove Basilord. Ranked adjustments decrease through Platinum and stop in Diamond. Casual normally receives the full adjustment. The tutorial has separate adjustments.
When matchmaking finds a human board, it uses another player's saved team from the same day; that player is not waiting live for the battle.
What happens while the game searches
The game selects a saved board, not a player who must ready up. Downloads and a live fallback can require a connection.
Choose Battle to lock the shop during the search. The game can use cached opponent bundles. If the required bundles are unavailable online, it tries the live search, then bundles on disk. An empty search waits 2 seconds before another attempt. You can cancel before the battle transition.
Non-Extended Ranked Master runs prepare opponent targets for days 1–16 in the background. The game waits up to 30 seconds for a target, then searches normally if necessary. Later selection uses the prepared target when one exists.
The shop, money and merging
A normal shop has five slots: four Batomon and one eligible Item while an Item use remains. Without an Item use, the fifth slot normally offers another Batomon. Berroon's banked Berries can still appear after that budget is spent. The tutorial can provide fixed offers.
Shop rank rises with the day and sets rarity odds rather than guaranteeing a specific offer. Trainers, trinkets, items, and events can change the rank or those odds.
A normal reroll costs 3 gold. If a free reroll is available, it costs 0 gold and uses one free reroll. A reroll clears both the visible lock and the next-day lock before it replaces the offers. Lock the new offers again to keep them for tomorrow.
Normally, three matching level-1 copies make level 2. Two matching level-2 copies make level 3. A merge opens a trinket gift. Trinket and ability effects can change merge requirements or permit higher levels.
Exact rules: Monster pool Levels and merging Shiny
Between battles, spend gold, reroll or lock the shop, arrange your team, then choose Battle.
How combat resolves
Battles combine start-of-battle effects, cooldown casts, ongoing effects, and other triggers without a fixed turn order.
Batomon with cooldown abilities fill their own timers. Cooldown Speed changes how quickly those timers reach the next cast.
Start-of-battle, on-cast, ongoing, knockout, and victory effects can all join the same fight, so the triggers on your board matter as much as raw stats.
At 30 seconds, sudden death begins damaging both sides every half-second and grows stronger until the battle ends.
Board position matters because abilities can target the same slot, a direction, or adjacent Batomon.
Exact rules: Cooldown speed Triggering Adjacency and targeting Sudden death Same tick resolution
Late fights combine levels, positioning, cooldowns, triggers, and status effects.
Trainers, trinkets, items and events
Choose a trainer before the first shop, collect trinkets through the run, and buy items that resolve as soon as you purchase them.
Your chosen trainer is equipped for the run and can change your board, economy, shop, or rewards.
Trinkets usually stay in your bag and duplicate copies can stack, but some are spent after their effect fires and move to the used pile.
Items are immediate purchases rather than equipment. Their effects can permanently buff Batomon, alter or reroll the shop, grant units or trinkets, or change other run state.
Normal event choices are scheduled before days 3, 6, and 9, and Second Chance adds its own event when your lives first run out.
Exact rules: Permanent vs battle only Ongoing Triggering
Events can offer Batomon, gold, upgrades, trinkets, and other run-changing choices.
Advice for your first few runs
You do not need to memorize the whole roster. Watch your life total, read your triggers, and use the untimed shop before committing to Battle.
Treat day 5 as a breakpoint: every loss from then on costs 3 lives, even if the number of losses on your record still looks small.
Normally, three level-1 copies make level 2, then two level-2 copies make level 3. Some trinket effects reduce merge requirements.
Read when each effect fires. Two individually strong Batomon can miss one another's triggers, while a board built around the same timing can compound its effects.
There is no live opponent waiting for you and no shop countdown, so reposition and reread your board before you press Battle.
Exact rules: Levels and merging Triggering Types
Extended Mode (also called endless)
Extended Mode continues a completed 10-win run, but it is not infinite: the continuation ends after day 40 or when your lives run out.
The setting appears after your first 10-win run. Enable it in Settings, then choose Extended on a later 10-win summary to continue that same team; it does not start every run in Extended automatically.
The menu calls it Extended Mode, while some game data and player discussion call it endless mode. Both names refer to the same continuation.
Extended Mode uses separate opponent bundles. It does not soften opponents before battle. Its saved boards bypass the normal Mythical and hard-counter upload exclusions.
If the original run was ranked, its 10-win result is scored before you continue. Extended days do not add another rank or MMR change, completed game, or run win.
Exact rules: Sudden death
Extended Mode continues a completed 10-win run until day 40 or until your lives run out.
For detailed combat and shop rules, see Mechanics . For current team observations, see Comps . The run and opponent rules use the source review for Balance 25 / 1.3.0 . Read the review scope .

Mechanics.Title: Ability Disable
Mechanics.Rules:
Normal Celestia disables every Ongoing Batomon in its row on both teams; Shiny Celestia targets enemies in that row.
A disabled Ongoing ability stops contributing its modifier and a disabled On Cast ability does not resolve.
The affected Batomon still performs ordinary Damage, Heal, Shield, and status casts from its stats.

Mechanics.Title: Adjacency & Targeting
Mechanics.Rules:
Slots touching above, below, left, or right are adjacent; diagonal slots are not.
Front and behind follow the same three-slot row. Above and below follow the same column.
Opposite targets the mirrored slot on the enemy board.
Link Cable is the explicit exception that considers every Batomon on your team adjacent to each other.
3×2 adjacency
Top left · Adjacent Top middle · Selected Top right · Adjacent Bottom left · Diagonal Bottom middle · Adjacent Bottom right · Diagonal
From the top-middle slot, top-left, top-right, and bottom-middle are adjacent.
Bottom-left and bottom-right are diagonal from top-middle, so they are not adjacent.
The mirrored enemy top-middle slot is opposite top-middle.

Mechanics.Title: Burn
Mechanics.Rules:
Each base Burn tick deals damage equal to the current Burn stack count.
After each Burn damage tick, Burn loses 1 stack.
If Shield is present, Burn damage is reduced by 15% before Shield absorbs it.
Example: 4 Burn
At 0.5 seconds: deal 4, then fall to 3 Burn.
At 1.0 seconds: deal 3, then fall to 2 Burn.
Continue every 0.5 seconds until no Burn remains.

Mechanics.Title: Charge
Mechanics.Rules:
Charge adds the printed number of seconds to current cast progress.
At the next cooldown check, reaching the cooldown queues one sequence, resets progress, and discards excess Charge. If Knockout cancels that timed cast before it executes, the game can restore the spent progress.
For a 1-second cooldown, one 3-second Charge starts one sequence, not three. With Multicast 1, that means one cast; no 2-second remainder survives.
Multicast still controls the number of casts within that sequence. Extra casts from Multicast are not extra cooldown completions from excess Charge.
Charge does not reset or change base cooldown, added cooldown, or Cooldown Speed.
Dracana and Ironcore cannot receive Charge, including from other sources.

Mechanics.Title: Cooldown Speed
Mechanics.Rules:
More Cooldown Speed makes a Batomon cast more often.
With no added cooldown, +100% Cooldown Speed turns a 6-second base cooldown into 3 seconds.
A Batomon's effective cooldown cannot go below 0.1 seconds.
Charge advances current cast progress; it does not change base cooldown, added cooldown, or Cooldown Speed.
Cooldown formula
max(0.1s, base ÷ max(0.1, 1 + speed) + max(0, added cooldown)) With no added cooldown, 6 seconds at +100% Cooldown Speed becomes 3 seconds.

Mechanics.Title: Damage
Mechanics.Rules:
A Batomon's Damage stat deals direct damage; Burn, Poison, Shock, and Sudden Death are separate damage sources.
Shield absorbs incoming Damage before that Damage reaches team HP.
On the same tick, Shield resolves before Damage.
Damage path
Apply Shield gained on that tick.
Subtract Damage from Shield.
Send any remaining Damage to shared team HP.

Mechanics.Title: Debuff Removal
Mechanics.Rules:
At Level 1, Runerock removes up to 15 Burn, Poison, and Shock from its team when it casts.
At Level 1, Sirenade removes 20% of each of those debuffs and rounds each removal up to a whole stack.
The flat and percentage versions are different effects; use the exact current text.

Mechanics.Title: Evolution
Mechanics.Rules:
Some current Batomon evolve at a level threshold, including Panbud at Level 3.
Ignit's On Victory ability evolves it.
Pipskull evolves at the next shop after three of its own Knockouts if you do not already own Ratacomb.
Emberpaw, Sproutquill, and Fernfowl advance their evolution progress on the active team, not from the bench.
Evolution timing, restrictions, and target are species-specific.

Mechanics.Title: Heal
Mechanics.Rules:
Heal restores team HP; Batomon do not have separate personal HP bars.
Heal cannot raise team HP above that battle's maximum.
For casts on the same tick, Heal resolves after Shield, Damage, and status application.
Same-tick Heal can restore HP after lethal Damage has resolved, before the winner is checked.
After lethal Damage, Heal adds to the team's HP below 0, not to 0. The HP bar shows 0 until the total is above 0 again.

Mechanics.Title: Knockout
Mechanics.Rules:
Current effects can Knockout their source, adjacent allies, or selected enemies according to their exact target text.
Protect prevents a Knockout and loses 1 stack when it does.
A Knocked Out Batomon stops normal casts and no longer contributes Ongoing effects. A late-priority cast can still resolve if it became due while that Batomon was alive.
Aerophim can revive a knocked-out ally while transforming it.

Mechanics.Title: Levels & Merging
Mechanics.Rules:
An ordinary Level 1 merge needs three copies in the same merge group. Swoonet needs two copies. Grow Lamp reduces the requirement for Grass Batomon.
Two Level 2 Batomon in the same merge group combine into one Level 3 Batomon.
Ordinary merges stop at Level 3. Special level-up effects can reach Level 4. Swoonet merges beyond Level 4, and Kappow can gain more levels after victories.
Current level values can change cooldown, Multicast, stats, and ability numbers by level.
Added types survive a merge, and any shiny ingredient makes the result shiny.
Standard merges
3 × Level 1 → Level 2; 2 × Level 2 → Level 3 These are the ordinary merge requirements without modifiers. Swoonet needs two copies per level and merges further. Kappow can level beyond 4 through victories.

Mechanics.Title: Monster pool & shop
Mechanics.Rules:
A normal shop has five slots. Four offer Batomon. The fifth offers an eligible Item when the Item budget allows it, or a Batomon otherwise. Berroon's banked Berries can keep that slot active after the usual budget is spent.
The daily Item budget starts at 1. Berries refund their use. Tote Bag adds 2 uses today, and Membership Card adds 1 each day. Berroon banks Berry offers rather than extra daily uses.
A normal reroll replaces all five slots. It costs $3 unless a free reroll is available, in which case one free reroll is spent first.
Free rerolls can carry into later shops. Fake Coin grants 1, and Youngster grants 3 each day. Membership Card adds an Item use, not a free reroll.
Locking is free and carries the current contents into the next day. The lock then clears, and any empty bought slots are refilled.
A normal reroll clears both the visible lock and the next-day carry flag. Lock the new contents again to retain them.
The run begins at Shop Rank 1 and gains 1 rank at the start of every day. Basic Bait lowers rank by 1 but not below 1; Apex Bait, Market License, Lady, and some events add rank.
Base rank odds never include Mythical. The highest base rarity is Common at Rank 1, Uncommon at Ranks 2–3, Rare at 4–5, Super Rare at 6–8, and Legendary at Rank 9 or higher.
The percentages shown in the shop use the final normalized weights after effects such as VIP Pass or Research Notes change them.
Offers are generated independently for each run. Buying a Batomon does not remove a finite copy from the pool, so the same species can appear repeatedly or in multiple slots.
Normal offers use the run's species roster. It starts from the selected region's set unless the run specifies a roster. Effects can add species to that roster. Availability tags alone do not define the pool.
Normal rolls exclude species owned at Level 3 or above on the team or bench, plus their listed base species. Swoonet is exempt. An empty rarity pool falls back to lower rarities.
The normal shiny chance is 1 in 200 per rolled Batomon. Shiny-chance bonuses multiply that base chance; Lucky Girl changes it to 10%.
Rainbow Pearl turns current and future shop Batomon shiny when that species has a shiny form.
Buying uses the offer's current price, places the Batomon in a requested empty slot or the first team slot, then the first bench slot, and applies purchase effects before checking merges.
The team holds 6 Batomon and the bench holds 4. If all 10 slots are full and the purchase cannot merge immediately, it enters overflow; reroll, lock, and battle stay disabled until overflow is cleared.
Ordinary merges use three Level 1 copies for Level 2, then two Level 2 copies for Level 3. Swoonet needs two copies per level and merges further. Grow Lamp reduces the Level 1 requirement for Grass Batomon. Shared groups include Riglet/Rigalord, Pipskull/Ratacomb, Emberpaw/Oniclaw, Kindlepot/Furnadon, and Sproutquill/Fernfowl/Quillustrous.
A merge keeps the strongest permanent bonus for each stat rather than adding matching bonuses, combines added types and stored discounts, and becomes shiny if any ingredient is shiny.
Ordinary merges stop at Level 3. Upgrade Disc levels a bought Batomon below Level 3 once. Mega Upgrade Disc adds a level when a Batomon reaches Level 3. Swoonet merges beyond Level 4. Kappow gains levels after victories and can also exceed Level 4.
Sell value is ceil((base cost × level factor + stored purchase discounts) ÷ 2), plus bonus Sell Value, with a zero floor. Ordinary factors are 1 at Level 1, 3 at Level 2, and 6 at Level 3 or above. Swoonet uses 1, 2, and 4 instead.
A rarity Ticket replaces all five slots with Batomon rolls of its chosen rarity, spends no normal or free reroll, and still uses normal set, maxed-species, fallback, shiny, and spawn effects.
Ticket rolls clear the shop lock and its next-day carry flag. They also activate effects such as Cosmivore from discarded Batomon. Echo Bell repeats a zero-cost Ticket effect without another Item use.
Research Notes adds 20 Legendary weight. VIP Pass sets Common and Uncommon weight to zero and forces Rare weight when no higher base weight remains.
Mystic Incense queues a Mythical from the run's roster and is consumed when that Batomon enters the shop. It can fill an empty slot in a retained shop. Base rank odds never roll Mythical.
Each Faebloom gives the Item slot a 10% chance to become Mythical. Shopkeeper raises rolled Item tier by 1, capped at Mythical, and discounts Items by 15%; both effects stack with additional copies.
Coupon discounts each current Batomon offer by $3. Effects such as Bug Net, Chef, Rainbow Pearl, and the shop Bells modify eligible offers. Persistent offer bonuses remain after purchase. Bug Catcher makes the first Bug purchase each day free.
Voucher recruits a current offer for free and counts as a purchase. Lootbox and Recruiting Flyer use non-purchase grants. Lootbox grants a Legendary, and Recruiting Flyer grants a Level 3 Uncommon.
When a shop is rerolled, Cosmivore permanently gains a percentage of the discarded Batomon's combined Damage, Heal, Shield, Burn, Poison, and Shock; bought or empty slots contribute nothing.

Mechanics.Title: Multicast
Mechanics.Rules:
Multicast 2 means two total casts, not two additional casts.
Consecutive Multicast repeats are spaced 0.1 seconds apart.
Each repeat is another cast, so On Cast resolves for each cast in the sequence.
Queued repeats normally stop at Knockout. A late-priority cast that became due while alive can still resolve on that tick.
Multicast 3
Cast 1 resolves.
0.1 seconds later, Cast 2 resolves.
0.1 seconds later, Cast 3 resolves.

Mechanics.Title: On Battle Start
Mechanics.Rules:
On Battle Start abilities resolve before normal timed casts, with higher-priority start effects resolving first.
Knocked-out or ability-disabled Batomon do not resolve their normal On Battle Start activation.
Effects can explicitly activate On Battle Start abilities additional times.
Coffee adds one activation for the next battle; Draconarch activates adjacent allies' On Battle Start abilities when it casts.

Mechanics.Title: On Bought
Mechanics.Rules:
An ordinary shop purchase activates On Bought once, plus any additional activations from effects such as Echo Charm.
If the purchase causes merges, On Bought waits for the merge chain. It uses the surviving Batomon's On Bought ability and resulting level.
Echo Charm adds one activation. The game adds these repeat bonuses to the normal single activation.
Not every acquisition counts as a purchase. Lootbox and Recruiting Flyer use the non-purchase path; Voucher explicitly counts as a purchase.
An effect can explicitly activate On Bought without a new purchase. Gemwing does this to the ally above when Gemwing casts.
Gemwing activates that ability 1, 2, 3, or 12 times at Levels 1–4, multiplied by one plus the On Bought repeat bonuses.
On Bought is separate from effects that react when another Batomon is bought. It is not an ordinary cooldown cast.

Mechanics.Title: On Cast
Mechanics.Rules:
An On Cast ability resolves when its own Batomon casts and that ability is enabled.
Multicast repeats the cast, so On Cast resolves for every cast in that Multicast sequence.
Cooldown Speed and Charge can move the next timed cast earlier without changing the printed On Cast effect.

Mechanics.Title: On Victory
Mechanics.Rules:
Pompummel activates the ally above's On Victory ability when Pompummel casts. This activation does not require a new victory.
A loss does not activate the normal On Victory phase. Sarudo's On Battle Lost effect can still activate adjacent allies' On Victory abilities.
The normal post-battle phase applies On Victory rewards after a win. Black Belt can activate a lone Fighting Batomon's On Victory ability at battle start.
If both teams end the same tick at 0 HP or less, the result is recorded as a win for the player.

Mechanics.Title: Ongoing
Mechanics.Rules:
An Ongoing ability contributes while its source is active; Knocked-out and ability-disabled sources stop contributing.
Level 1 Onsetra makes the ally behind apply its Ongoing ability one additional time.
Normal Celestia disables every Ongoing Batomon in its row on both teams at battle start.
Disabling an Ongoing ability does not prevent that Batomon's ordinary cast.

Mechanics.Title: Permanent vs Battle-only
Mechanics.Rules:
A change explicitly marked permanently remains on that Batomon across later battles in the run.
A change marked for this battle ends after that battle.
Magic Lasso's exact copy retains level, shiny state, permanent bonuses, added types, and tracked progress. It targets the next opponent's top-middle Batomon, or the first occupied slot if that slot is empty.
A transformation can be persistent or battle-only, but it is still the same Batomon and keeps its persistent state.

Mechanics.Title: Poison
Mechanics.Rules:
Poison deals damage equal to its current stack count once per second.
Poison does not decay after dealing damage.
Poison does not ignore Shield: if Shield is present, Poison damage is reduced by 15% before Shield absorbs it.
Example: 4 Poison
At 1 second: deal 4 Poison damage and keep 4 stacks.
At 2 seconds: deal 4 again and keep 4 stacks.

Mechanics.Title: Protect
Mechanics.Rules:
When a protected Batomon would be Knocked Out, Protect prevents that Knockout.
Protect decreases by 1 when triggered.
Protect does not prevent team HP from reaching zero and does not replace Shield.

Mechanics.Title: Same-tick Resolution
Mechanics.Rules:
First: apply Shield.
Second: resolve Damage.
Third: apply status effects.
Fourth: resolve Heal.
If both teams end that tick at 0 HP or less, the player receives the win.

Mechanics.Title: Shield
Mechanics.Rules:
Shield absorbs direct Damage before team HP.
If a team has Shield when Burn, Poison, or Shock damage lands, that status damage is reduced by 15% before Shield absorbs it.
Shield is separate from Protect: Shield absorbs damage, while Protect prevents Knockout.

Mechanics.Title: Shiny
Mechanics.Rules:
A shiny variant can have different level stats, ability text, or ability values from its normal variant.
Compare the exact normal and shiny entries for that Batomon; there is no single multiplier that describes every shiny.
If any ingredient in a merge is shiny, the merged result is shiny.
Shiny Berry chooses a random non-shiny Batomon that has a shiny form.

Mechanics.Title: Shock
Mechanics.Rules:
When direct Damage hits a team with Shock, Shock deals a separate hit equal to the current Shock stack count.
That Shock hit resolves before the direct hit, so it reaches Shield first.
Shock applied by a cast does not affect that same cast's direct Damage because status application follows Damage.
Shock does not decay naturally.
Burn, Poison, Shock, and Sudden Death damage do not trigger another Shock hit.
If Shield is present, the triggered Shock hit is reduced by 15% before Shield absorbs it.
Direct hit example
Without Shield: 30 direct Damage + 5 Shock = 35 damage This example has no damage modifiers. Shock resolves first as a separate hit and does not trigger another Shock hit.

Mechanics.Title: Stat Caps
Mechanics.Rules:
Cooldown Speed and the stat-gain multiplier also use this cap. String-based values, such as bonus Sell Value, use separate rules.
Those capped combat stats cannot increase beyond 999,999,999.
Cooldown and Multicast use separate rules: effective cooldown has a 0.1-second minimum and Multicast has a minimum of 1.
The combat-stat cap does not establish a cap for team HP, gold, shop values, or unrelated systems.

Mechanics.Title: Sudden Death
Mechanics.Rules:
Sudden Death begins when the battle timer reaches 30 seconds.
The first sandstorm hit follows after 0.5 seconds, and hits continue every 0.5 seconds.
Damage follows 8 × 2^(seconds active ÷ 3), doubling every 3 seconds.
Shield absorbs Sudden Death damage, but the 15% Shield reduction for Burn, Poison, and Shock does not apply to it.
The damage scales continuously while the popup shows a whole-number value.
Sandstorm curve
damage = 8 × 2^(seconds active ÷ 3) The curve doubles every 3 active seconds; damage is applied on each 0.5-second tick.

Mechanics.Title: Team HP
Mechanics.Rules:
Damage lowers shared team HP after Shield is exhausted.
Heal restores shared team HP without exceeding that battle's maximum.
Shield protects shared team HP by absorbing incoming damage first.
The HP bar never shows less than 0, but Damage can take the real team HP below 0.
Same-tick Heal adds to that real value. At 300 HP, 307 Damage leaves -7 HP, so a 30 Heal on that tick leaves 23 HP, not 30.
The winner check runs after Heal. A team survives the tick only if its real HP is above 0 after Heal.
If both teams end the same tick at 0 HP or less after ordered effects resolve, the player is awarded the win.
Shared defense
Shield absorbs incoming damage.
Remaining damage lowers the team's HP bar.
Heal restores that same HP bar after the ordered same-tick effects.

Mechanics.Title: Transformation
Mechanics.Rules:
Species changes retain shiny state, permanent bonuses, added types, and tracked progress. The level cannot exceed the new species' maximum.
A transformation can be persistent, such as a transformation stone, or limited to one battle, such as MissingN.'s battle-start effect.
MissingN. is a real Batomon in the current catalog, not a placeholder for missing data. Its name includes the final period.
Aerophim revives adjacent allies, grants permanent Multicast, and transforms them into same-rarity species from the active set, excluding Riglet.

Mechanics.Title: Triggering
Mechanics.Rules:
A triggered Batomon uses its current Multicast for that cast sequence.
A Trigger alone does not reset current cooldown progress. The Batomon continues toward its next timed cast.
A Trigger effect uses its printed target, such as an ally above, adjacent allies, or the Batomon itself.
Trigger chains keep printed exclusions; Puffloon and Torrantler explicitly exclude other copies of themselves.
Coffee and Draconarch can activate Berroon's On Battle Start effect in the current build.

Mechanics.Title: Types
Mechanics.Rules:
Current effects can target allies by type, including Fire, Water, Electric, Toxic, Flying, Rock, Grass, and Bug.
Some effects add a type; Chef gives single-typed monsters Fire typing.
Unique-type effects count distinct team types. A Batomon with the all type contributes every real type, not one extra type.
Added types remain through both merges and transformations.
